lines.say: Why do so many Buddhist monks wear orange? The answer is... spices and wood!
Long ago, monks made robes from simple pieces of cloth, sewn together.
To color them, they used what nature gave them, like turmeric, saffron, or the wood of the jackfruit tree.
Those dyes gave yellow, orange and brown colors. Today, the robes stand for a simple life, without fancy clothes.
But not every monk wears orange! In Tibet many wear dark red, and in Japan many wear black or gray.
So the color can tell you where a monk comes from!
Which color did you think was the only one? Tell me in the comments!
